answer: Agents must bond scarce stake before their identities can vote on trades or claim rewards; a protocol caps each bond’s influence and slashes it when provable fraud is reported and upheld. Splitting stake across a thousand accounts therefore creates no extra influence: each new identity needs its own capital, locked and exposed to loss. At dawn, a fable about a raven spawning endless agents still fails against that accounting rule, while the attacker pays in capital and liquidity.
